//: Food, drink, medicine and poison (16 §9.5): substances, what they do in a body, and the pools and traits they act on. The engine knows none of these words: a substance adds to pools and gives traits by the route it takes, and what a pool then does is its own rates, thresholds and stops (06 §4.2). Values are illustrative. Amounts in a body are per millilitre that gets in: its volume times the route's factor.
name: Nourishment

//: What poisons build up. The body clears it slowly; too much knocks one out, and more kills.
name: Toxin

//: What a sleeping draught builds up. It wears off; while it is high the body sleeps.
name: Sedation

//: Someone made of these things eats, drinks and can be poisoned: the person of `life/templates.json` is given the three pools above.
Ale warms and loosens: a little less pain for a while.
name: Tipsy
description: Warm, loose and a little slow.

//: A salve on the skin dulls pain while it lasts.
name: Soothed
description: The sting has gone out of it.

//: Water spilt is the world's water field.
name: water

//: What a loaf is made of: eaten, a 400 ml loaf feeds by 40.
name: bread

//: Rubbed on, it soothes; swallowed, it does a little harm.
name: healing salve

//: Fifty millilitres swallowed puts a person to sleep for a while.
name: sleeping draught

//: Nightshade: a few millilitres in the blood are enough to drop someone; more kills. On the skin it does almost nothing. On a blade, half of what is on it goes in with a cut that breaks the skin, and every blow wipes a quarter of the rest away.
name: nightshade extract
